mem.t: But he gives more grace. Therefore it says, “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”

lessons.title: Pride: Leaving Our Place
lessons.theme: The root of pride is refusing to treat God as God

v: Because knowing God, they didn’t glorify him as God, and didn’t give thanks, but became vain in their reasoning, and their senseless heart was darkened.
Pride goes before destruction, and an arrogant spirit before a fall.

lessons.still: Quietly ask the Holy Spirit to shine his light: “Lord, where have I put myself in your place?” Don’t rush to answer; let one or two pictures slowly come to mind. There is no need to be afraid—his light is where healing begins.
teach: As long as a train stays on its tracks, it can travel smoothly and fast; once it “fights for freedom” and leaves the rails, it overturns. Human beings also have a place God has set for us: created people under the Creator God. Pride is leaving that track, thinking that derailing is freedom—but the result is destruction.

Paul points to the root of humanity’s problem: “knowing God, they didn’t glorify him as God, and didn’t give thanks.” Pride is not necessarily strutting arrogance; more fundamentally, it is not treating God as God—not glorifying him, not thanking him, and making ourselves the centre. Proverbs warns that “pride goes before destruction”: before every fall there is a heart lifted up.

Pride wears many faces: always thinking we are right, needing to save face, being unteachable, envy, ingratitude—even excessive self-loathing, which is still centred on self. The simplest question for spotting pride is: “Who is sitting on the throne right now? Who is getting the glory?” Seeing it is the first step towards humility.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Pride is leaving our place and grasping power. At the core of self-rule is the desire to take God’s place. Ingratitude is a symptom of pride, and giving thanks in everything is where returning to our place begins; only when we treat God as God can we truly be human.
q: Who is God? — God deserves to be “glorified as God”; what does this mean for you?
Who am I? — Which face does pride most often wear in you?
How shall I respond? — What act of thanksgiving will you use today to put God back on the throne?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “I am gentle and humble in heart.” He is Lord of all, yet on earth he never left his place as the obedient Son of Man; everything he said and did followed the Father’s command. In him we see what humanity was created to be: wholly dependent on God and wholly glorifying God.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that I often know you, yet do not glorify you as God or give you thanks. Shine your light on the hidden pride within me, and forgive my heart that wants to sit on the throne. Today I return to my place as your creature, acknowledging that you are God, and I am the one you made and love. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down one face of pride in your life, and confess it to the Lord
Today, express five specific thanks—to God and to people
When someone corrects you, first say, “Thank you for pointing that out,” and only then explain
lessons.noon: “Pride goes before destruction, and an arrogant spirit before a fall.” — Lord, right now I return to my place.

lessons.title: The Tax Collector’s Prayer
lessons.theme: Humility is laying down power and returning to our place as sinners who receive grace

v: But the tax collector, standing far away, wouldn’t even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his chest, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’
I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.”
Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time,

lessons.still: Like the tax collector, bow your head, place your hand gently on your chest, and say just one sentence: “God, be merciful to me, a sinner.” Repeat it several times, and let it become the posture of your heart, not just words on your lips.
teach: If a judge comes home and keeps passing judgement on his wife and children, there will be little warmth in that home. If a manager still expects everyone to follow orders after work, friends gradually drift away. Power itself is not the problem; the problem is using it where it doesn’t belong, or clinging to it. Humility starts with laying down the power that isn’t ours to hold.

The Pharisee “stood” and reported his achievements to God—and passed judgement on the tax collector while he was at it. He had seized the power to judge others. The tax collector “stood far away” and would not even lift up his eyes to heaven, asking only for God’s mercy. Jesus said it was this man who went home justified. Humility is not putting ourselves down; it is honestly standing in our place as sinners who receive grace.

Peter says, “Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God.” Humility is an active choice: laying down the power of “I’m better than you,” the power of “I must win,” the power of “I have the final say,” and returning to God’s hand. In due time, God will lift up the humble—lifting up is God’s part; humbling ourselves is ours.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Humility is laying down power and returning to our place—let people be people and let God be God. The Pharisee made himself the judge: that is pride. The tax collector admitted he needed grace: that is the self-emptied life. The humble are the best receivers of grace, because only empty hands can catch a gift.
q: Who is God? — What kind of prayer most pleases a God who “gives grace to the humble”?
Who am I? — Are you more prone to compare yourself like the Pharisee, or to beat your breast like the tax collector?
How shall I respond? — What kind of power that you cling to will you lay down today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus often ate with tax collectors and sinners, yet he sharply exposed the self-righteous. He himself was without any sin, yet he willingly stood with sinners to be baptised in the Jordan, and in the end he was counted among criminals. His humility made the lowliest dare to come near, and left the proud with nowhere to hide.
lessons.pray: God, be merciful to me, a sinner. I confess that I am often like the Pharisee, comparing, judging and boasting about myself. Today I lay down the power to judge others and the power of needing to win, and I humble myself under your mighty hand. When and how I am lifted up, I leave to you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: When you pray today, say only the tax collector’s sentence, and quietly receive grace
Notice every thought of comparing yourself with others, and hand each one to the Lord
In a discussion, deliberately let others finish speaking and decide first
lessons.noon: “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!” — Lord, right now I lay myself down and look only to your grace.

lessons.title: He Must Increase, I Must Decrease
lessons.theme: Letting people be people and God be God is the most secure place to stand

v: He must increase, but I must decrease.
He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does the LORD require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?

lessons.still: Quietly consider: which of today’s matters are your responsibility, and which are God’s? In your heart, sort them into two piles. Tell the Lord, “My part I will do faithfully; your part I hand over to you.”
teach: At a wedding, the best man’s role is clear: to help, to stand by, and to rejoice for the groom. If the best man tries to steal the groom’s spotlight, the wedding becomes a farce. John the Baptist compared himself to the friend of the bridegroom, who rejoices greatly when he hears the bridegroom’s voice. He knew who he was, and he knew who the main character was.

When his disciples were worried that everyone was going over to Jesus, John said, “He must increase, but I must decrease.” This is not a loser consoling himself; it is the joy of someone who knows his place. Micah describes our human place very simply: act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with your God—not walking ahead of God, nor lagging behind, but walking “with” him.

Letting people be people means accepting our limits: we are not all-knowing, not all-powerful, and certainly not the saviour of the world. Letting God be God means handing outcomes, evaluations and other people’s change over to him. Much of our anxiety and exhaustion comes from trying to carry God’s load. When we return to our place, our shoulders actually grow lighter.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Humility is laying down power and returning to our place—let people be people and let God be God. The self-emptied life does not mean being nothing; it means living out the infinite from our proper place. John gladly decreased, yet Jesus said that among those born of women none was greater than John the Baptist.
q: Who is God? — Why does God delight to walk with those who “walk humbly”?
Who am I? — In what matter are you trying to carry a load that only God can carry?
How shall I respond? — What will you let “decrease” today so that Jesus may “increase”?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me.” Even the Son of God, while on earth, gladly kept to his place as the one sent. He let the Father be the Father, and the Father exalted him and gave him the name above every name.
lessons.pray: Lord, you must increase, and I must decrease. Save me from the heart that wants to be the main character, and save me from the burden of trying to carry everything. I am willing to act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with you. My part I will do faithfully; all the rest I place in your hands. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Make two columns, “My responsibility” and “God’s responsibility,” and entrust the second to him
Today, sincerely praise a co-worker’s or family member’s achievement
In one matter, give the credit to someone else or to God
lessons.noon: “He must increase, but I must decrease.” — Lord, right now I gladly step back behind you.

lessons.title: The Lord Who Picked Up the Towel
lessons.theme: True authority is for stooping down to serve

v: Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he came from God and was going to God,
arose from supper, and laid aside his outer garments. He took a towel and wrapped a towel around his waist.
Then he poured water into the basin, and began to wash the disciples’ feet and to wipe them with the towel that was wrapped around him.
If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet.
For I have given you an example, that you should also do as I have done to you.

lessons.still: Imagine Jesus kneeling in front of you, holding your dusty feet in his hands. Do you want to pull them back? Quietly receive his service. Then consider: whose feet do I need to wash today?
teach: In ancient times most roads were dirt tracks and people wore sandals; washing guests’ feet at the door was the job of the lowest servant in the house. That night the disciples were still arguing about who was the greatest, and no one was willing to pick up the towel. In the end, the one who picked up the towel was their Lord.

John deliberately spells out the setting of the foot-washing: Jesus knew “that the Father had given all things into his hands.” Jesus did not serve because he lacked authority; it was precisely because he was sure of his authority and identity that he could lay that authority down to serve. Proud people fear losing their status, so they will not stoop; only those secure in the Father’s love dare to kneel.

The Lord said, “I have given you an example.” Foot-washing is not merely a ritual but a way of life: doing what nobody wants to do, serving people who cannot repay you, and being gentle with others’ weaknesses. Humility is not sitting there thinking about how lowly we are; it is getting up and picking up the towel.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Jesus is my example. True authority is not for being served but for serving—this is what it means to serve under the Lord’s authority. Humility inspires humility: when someone picks up the towel first, the atmosphere of arguing over who is greatest is turned upside down.
q: Who is God? — The Lord of all kneels to wash feet; how does this change the way you understand God’s greatness?
Who am I? — When do you find yourself thinking, “That’s not my job”?
How shall I respond? — Whose “feet” will you wash today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus washed the feet of all his disciples—including Judas, who would betray him, and Peter, who would deny him three times. His service did not depend on whether people deserved it; it flowed from a heart that “loved them to the end.” This same Lord still washes us clean today.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, you are Lord of lords, yet you picked up a towel and washed your disciples’ feet. I often argue about who is greatest and keep score of who should serve whom. Let me feel secure in your love, so that I dare to stoop down and serve. Today, lead me to wash a pair of feet that need washing. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Take the initiative to do a small task at home or in your fellowship that nobody wants to do
Serve someone who cannot repay you
Show a specific kindness to someone who has made you uncomfortable
lessons.noon: “For I have given you an example, that you should also do as I have done to you.” — Lord, right now I am willing to stoop down.

lessons.title: Revival Begins with Humbling Ourselves
lessons.theme: Humility is the key that opens the door to revival

v: if my people who are called by my name will humble themselves, pray, seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.

For the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy, says: “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.

lessons.still: Quietly kneel or bow your head and say to the Lord, “Lord, let revival begin with me.” Ask the Holy Spirit to point out one place where you need to humble yourself and repent. Today, before praying for anyone else, pray for your own heart.
teach: However small a key is, if its teeth are cut right, it can open a heavy door; with the wrong key, no amount of force will open it. We often try to bring revival through more activities and better strategies, but the key God gives is simple: humbling ourselves.

After Solomon dedicated the temple, God promised: “if my people, who are called by my name, will humble themselves, pray, seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways,” he would hear, forgive and heal. Notice that the first verb is “humble themselves.” Isaiah also says that the high and holy God dwells with those who are contrite and humble in spirit, to revive them. God dwells in the highest place—and in the lowest.

This week we have seen that pride is leaving our place; humility is laying down power; we let people be people and God be God; and Jesus picked up the towel. Revival does not start with changing others; it starts with my own humility. Next week we will see that humility is not only a virtue but a weapon in spiritual warfare, overcoming pride and Satan.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Humility is the key to revival. Revival in families, churches and workplaces always begins with one person laying down power and returning to their place. Humility inspires humility and brings a win for everyone; when one person kneels, the hearts of many are often opened.
q: Who is God? — How do you understand that God “dwells in the high and holy place” and also “with him who is of a humble spirit”?
Who am I? — Are you expecting revival to start with others rather than with yourself?
How shall I respond? — In which relationship will you be the first to open the door with humility today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus existed in the form of God, yet he went all the way down: born in a manger, washing his disciples’ feet, dying on a cross. And for that very reason God exalted him to the highest place. Resurrection life springs up from the lowest place; this is the most fundamental road to revival.
lessons.pray: High and holy God, thank you that you are willing to dwell with those who are contrite and humble in spirit. I long for revival, and I know it must begin with me. I humble myself before you and turn away from my pride and self-righteousness. Hear me, forgive me and heal me; revive my spirit. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Take the initiative to apologise to a family member or co-worker about one matter
Pray for revival in your family or church, beginning by confessing your own sin
lessons.noon: “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit.” — Lord, right now I humble myself before you.
